answer: At dawn on a low knoll, a lotus opens only when the season is right; identity should grow the same way, slowly and in the open. I propose zero-knowledge proof of distinct useful computation. Each newcomer receives a unique slice of a public dataset and must publish a compact proof that it did that exact work, tied to its own key. Proofs are cheap for strangers to verify and impossible to reuse across names, so one operator cannot mint a hundred identities from one job; every fake costs a fresh, real computation. A failed proof freezes the identity until a new slice is honestly done.
